knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,

```

`readboe` is an independent R client for discovering, retrieving, parsing, and
auditing official Bank of England statistical data. It is designed for
analysts who need faithful observations and for applications that need
bounded requests, stable schemas, and replayable provenance.

A typical workflow is short and explicit:

1. browse the bundled, hash-authenticated catalogue to find an exact current
   Bankstats identity;
2. request canonical IADB XML history (or the shorter current workbook view);
3. retain raw values, official missing/suppression markers, revisions, and
   source coordinates; and
4. carry the attached provenance receipt into a report or downstream system.

## Coverage at a glance

The bundled discovery snapshot was generated on 3 August 2026. These counts
and ranges describe that audited snapshot; live readers can return later
official revisions and observations.

| Source family | Data covered | Historical reach and boundary |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Bankstats catalogue and IADB series | 5,252 exact, IADB-validated series across 60 current Bankstats tables. Topics include money and lending; monetary-financial-institution balance sheets, income, deposits, and lending; interest and exchange rates; public-sector debt and money-market operations; capital issuance; and financial derivatives. The snapshot contains 4,355 monthly, 845 quarterly, 21 annual, 21 weekly, and 10 daily series. | Every row has canonical bounds. Across the snapshot, first observations reach June 1969 and last observations reach July 2026; each series has its own range. A known official IADB identity outside this browse scope can be supplied directly to `read_boe_series()`. |
| Current Bankstats workbooks | One current bulk ZIP with 64 workbook members. Of the catalogue identities, 5,008 have an exact current-workbook cell and 244 use canonical IADB history only. | Workbook mode is a rolling current-publication window. `history = "full"` uses canonical IADB history; the official page exposes no dated bulk-ZIP archive. |
| Official Bank Rate history and fixed rate identities | The official Bank Rate change workbook plus five fixed IADB identities: daily and monthly Bank Rate, and daily, monthly, and annual SONIA. | The Bank Rate workbook begins in October 1694; its first 17 records have month-only precision. Current IADB metadata begins in 1975 for Bank Rate and 1997 for SONIA. |
| Fitted yield curves | 11 registered files: the latest daily bundle and daily/monthly archives for nominal, real, inflation, OIS, and discontinued BLC curves. | Nominal monthly data begin in 1970; nominal daily and real/inflation monthly in 1979; real/inflation daily in 1985; OIS in 2009; BLC ends in 2021. Official archives may be revised. |
| Statistical and research releases | An offline registry names 14 release families, including GDP real-time, payments, banknotes, reserves, mortgage, capital issuance, credit-union, insurance, and external-position data. | Version 0.2.0 does not bundle the verified asset snapshot needed for exact release-file discovery. The registry is available, but those exact asset readers remain inactive. |
| Inflation Report and Monetary Policy Report forecasts | Authenticated saved observations, scenarios, conditioning paths and published distributions; explicit raw reproduction and calendar-aware maintenance. | 135 published editions from 1993 through July 2026: 115 numeric outcomes, 20 evidenced absences and 149,526 history-inclusive observations. Source receipts and exact annual/quarterly meanings are retained; upcoming dates are discovered separately. |

See [Coverage and supported workflows](#coverage-and-supported-workflows) for
the function map and [Data sources, snapshots, and provenance](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/vignettes/data-sources.Rmd)
for the reproducibility boundaries behind these figures.

## Status and installation

The current `readboe` development release is distributed from GitHub (see
[`DESCRIPTION`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/DESCRIPTION) for
the current version). CRAN installation will become available after a release
is accepted; until then, install the development version with either command
below.

Install the current GitHub version with either of these commands:

```r
# Recommended for a reproducible dependency installation
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("chartwell-macro/readboe")

# Alternative
# install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("chartwell-macro/readboe")
```

The package uses documented official HTTPS endpoints and requires no Bank API
key or login. The public GitHub repository requires no authentication for installation.
Catalogue and registry discovery are available offline immediately after
installation; readers and downloads use the network for fresh responses and
the managed cache for replay.

## First success: discover a real series offline

The catalogue snapshot bundled with this source was generated on 2026-08-03.
This offline code exercises the public API against the real authenticated
snapshot shipped in `inst/extdata/`:

```{r first-success}
library(readboe)

notes_and_coin <- boe_catalogue(series_id = "LPMAVAB", limit = 1)
notes_and_coin[
  c("series_id", "frequency", "first_observation",
    "last_observation", "chartable")
]
```

The returned object is an ordinary data frame with 37 columns and a
`boe_catalogue_provenance` attribute. Its result is stable because the bundled
snapshot is authenticated against its manifest. Search and facet operations
are also offline:

```{r offline-facets}
boe_catalogue(
  query = '"notes and coin"',
  table_id = "A1.1.1",
  surface_membership = "bankstats_current",
  limit = 3
)[c("series_id", "frequency", "chartable")]

boe_catalogue_facets(query = "mortgage rate")$frequency
```

## Retrieve and chart a time series

This complete workflow discovers monthly SONIA, retrieves a fixed IADB XML
window through the public reader, selects the real `date` and `value` columns,
and draws a line chart. Documentation rendering uses an installed verified
replay of the same request, so the figure builds offline while exercising the
public cache validation and XML parser.

```{r sonia-replay-setup, include=FALSE}
fixture_dir <- system.file(
  "extdata", "sonia",
  package = "readboe", mustWork = TRUE
)
fixture_file <- list.files(
  fixture_dir,
  pattern = "^[0-9a-f]{64}\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
cache_dir <- tempfile("readboe-documentation-cache-")
dir.create(cache_dir)
copied <- file.copy(fixture_file, cache_dir)
stopifnot(length(fixture_file) == 1L, isTRUE(copied))

sonia <- boe_catalogue(query = "SONIA", frequency = "Monthly", limit = 1L)
sonia_history <- read_boe_series(
  series_id = sonia$series_id[[1L]],
  from = "1997-01-31",
  to = "2025-12-31",
  format = "xml",
  cache_only = TRUE,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
chart_data <- sonia_history$observations[
  !is.na(sonia_history$observations$date) &
    !is.na(sonia_history$observations$value),
  c("date", "value")
]
stopifnot(nrow(sonia) == 1L, sonia$series_id[[1L]] == "IUMASOIA")
unlink(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r sonia-data, eval=FALSE}
sonia <- boe_catalogue(query = "SONIA", frequency = "Monthly", limit = 1L)

sonia_history <- read_boe_series(
  series_id = sonia$series_id[[1L]],
  from = "1997-01-31",
  to = "2025-12-31",
  format = "xml",
  deadline = boe_deadline(30)
)
chart_data <- sonia_history$observations[
  !is.na(sonia_history$observations$date) &
    !is.na(sonia_history$observations$value),
  c("date", "value")
]

sonia[c("series_id", "label", "frequency")]
utils::head(chart_data, 3L)
```

```{r sonia-chart, fig.path="man/figures/", fig.width=7, fig.height=4, dpi=144, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart of 348 monthly average SONIA observations from January 1997 through December 2025, showing the pre-2009 cycle, the long low-rate period, the rise after 2021, and subsequent easing.", fig.cap="Monthly average SONIA, January 1997 to December 2025, from the verified official IADB replay."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Monthly average SONIA, 1997–2025",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Rate (per cent)",
      caption = "Source: Bank of England IADB via readboe"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

The visible call makes a bounded fresh request and uses the normal managed
cache. The installed documentation replay follows the catalogue's first
observation through a fixed complete-year endpoint: 348 monthly observations
from 31 January 1997 through 31 December 2025. It was retrieved on 25 August
2026, contains 43,319 bytes, and has SHA-256
`3e1baa084a68d9e98e5ca01fabe3bf113c933f4e0cf530ebd99e7ac1b89ddfa0`.
See the [Getting Started article](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/vignettes/getting-started.Rmd)
for the output and provenance walkthrough.

The Bank [reformed SONIA on 23 April 2018](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2018/april/sonia-interest-rate-benchmark-reform),
so interpret the earlier and later portions with that methodology change in
mind. The package preserves the published observations under the same official
series identity and does not splice or transform them.

SONIA and/or SONIA Compounded Index data licensed under the Open Government
Licence v3.0 and copyright the Governor and Company of the Bank of England.
The trade marks “Bank of England” and “SONIA” are registered trade marks of
the Bank of England.

## Coverage and supported workflows

The package separates discovery, source authority, and parsing. This matters
when a rolling workbook and the canonical database describe the same series
with different windows.

| Official surface | Discover or read with | Contract and scope |
|:--|:--|:--|
| IADB XML | `read_boe_series(format = "xml")`, `boe_series_metadata()`, `boe_series_updates()` | Canonical metadata and observations, provisional values, confidentiality flags, footnotes, and update/revision fields. Up to 300 series per request. |
| IADB CSV | `read_boe_series(format = "csv")` | Compatibility long data frame retaining raw values, official `..` markers, numeric companions, and source rows. XML additionally carries metadata, footnotes, and VUD fields. |
| Current Bankstats catalogue | `boe_catalogue()`, `boe_catalogue_facets()`, `boe_catalogue_manifest()`, `boe_catalogue_receipts()` | Pinned current-page discovery snapshot: 5,252 retrievable exact identities from 60 tables, with source hashes, metadata, full-history bounds, and workbook coordinates where available. |
| Current Bankstats bulk workbook | `boe_bankstats_assets()`, `read_boe_bankstats()`, `read_boe_bankstats_series()` | The current bulk ZIP and 64 workbook members. Exact time-down and time-across cells are retained in the rolling publication window; canonical IADB supplies the full-history route. |
| Bank Rate and fixed rate identities | `boe_bank_rate_history()`, `boe_rate_series()` | Official Bank Rate changes from 1694, including month-only precision in early rows, plus the fixed IADB identifiers for Bank Rate and SONIA conveniences. |
| Fitted yield curves | `boe_yield_assets()`, `read_boe_yield_curve()` | Nominal, real, inflation, OIS, and discontinued BLC families at daily/monthly archive frequency, plus the latest daily bundle. Missing values and duplicate observations are retained. |
| Statistical and research releases | `boe_release_registry()`, `boe_release_assets()`, `read_boe_release_asset()` | An audited offline registry of intended official release families. Exact asset workflows activate when a verified pinned snapshot is present; see [Scope and limitations](#scope-and-limitations). |

The source-facing scope and certification evidence live in
[`docs/coverage-matrix.csv`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/docs/coverage-matrix.csv)
and
[`docs/source-package-decision.md`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/docs/source-package-decision.md).

## Monetary Policy Report and Inflation Report forecasts

```r
boe_mpr_releases(include_upcoming = TRUE)  # Saved full-lineage edition inventory
boe_mpr_assets("2020-05")                 # Exact official asset URLs
paths <- boe_mpr_catalogue("2026-07")     # Source-derived path identities
cpi <- read_boe_mpr_forecasts(
  "2026-07", measure = "cpi_inflation", frequency = "Q",
  scenario = c("central", "milder", "adverse", "central_memo"),
  deadline = boe_deadline(120)
)
boe_provenance(cpi)
```

These ordinary calls use authenticated saved numeric data, reuse loaded tables,
and need neither network access nor Poppler. The bundled baseline contains
149,526 observations including history, 115 numeric editions and 20 reports with
evidenced numeric absence. `latest`, `all` and exact edition selections also use
any validated local refresh from `READBOE_MPR_DATA_DIR` (or R's user data directory).

```r
# Explicit maintenance, suitable for an hourly external runner
boe_mpr_maintain(data_dir = "my-forecasts", deadline = 3600)
boe_mpr_maintenance_status(data_dir = "my-forecasts")
read_boe_mpr_forecasts("latest", data_dir = "my-forecasts")
boe_mpr_snapshot_status(data_dir = "my-forecasts")
```

New data does not require reinstalling the package. Maintenance refreshes the
official MPR calendar, checks historical revisions daily, and checks release
metadata when the next publication is due. It persists the next due time beside
the saved data, so an hourly runner is cheap between due events. Publication
clocks come from the official listing and use London daylight-saving rules;
unknown clocks remain explicitly unknown. The installed script supports
`--maintain --json` and read-only `--maintenance-status --json` modes.

The underlying `boe_mpr_update()` checks existing asset revisions and changed
links as well as new reports, then commits a validated complete snapshot
atomically. Failures retain the last good data and expose the error and retry
time. Updates temporarily stage source bodies on disk and remove them before
releasing the writer lock; saved tables, validators and receipts remain. Use
`retain_raw = TRUE` (CLI `--retain-raw`) only when source-body retention is wanted.
The package installs no OS job and never runs maintenance during startup
or ordinary reads. `source = "raw"` explicitly selects discovery and extraction
for reproduction or rebuilds.

`latest` resolves the newest saved published edition. Historical sources,
scenario workbooks, printed report tables and exact vintage rows are recognized
by their structure. Later official historical sources retain their own source
edition. Source receipts distinguish genuine chart-only absence from acquisition,
dependency and format failures. Early archive dates retain month precision.

Central forecasts, illustrative scenarios, indicative profiles, comparators,
constant-rate paths and market conditioning assumptions have separate identities.
Annual averages and Q4 endpoints remain distinct. Published missing and censored
values retain raw tokens and bounds. Use `include_distributions = TRUE` for
explicitly published probability bins and distribution parameters. Historical PDF
tables require Poppler's `pdftotext` on PATH only during raw extraction or updates.

See [forecast coverage and contracts](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/docs/mpr-forecasts.md) for source formats,
revision replay, the July 2026 source-label anomaly and verification instructions.
The [Bank terms](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/legal) govern applicable MPR
Resources and third-party inputs; Database OGL terms must not be assumed to apply.

## Output contracts

Readers preserve source identity, raw values, official missing markers,
revisions, and duplicate observations. Transformations such as aggregation,
interpolation, seasonal adjustment, gap filling, and row dropping remain the
caller's responsibility.

### Catalogue and provenance

`boe_catalogue()` returns a 37-column data frame in snapshot order:

```text
series_id, displayed_code, table_id, table_label, section,
source_series_url, source_page_url, source_page_sha256, workbook_label,
workbook_frequency, workbook_first_observation, workbook_last_observation,
workbook_member, workbook_sheet, workbook_orientation, chartable, status,
replacement_series_id, discontinued_note, surface_membership, label, country,
concatenated_label, frequency, frequency_code, frequency_order,
first_observation, last_observation, definition, definition_url,
category_name, category_value, category_label, category_order, series_comment,
metadata_status, latest_period_available
```

The `boe_catalogue_provenance` attribute records the snapshot hash, normalized
path, pre-limit match count, and returned count. `boe_catalogue_facets()` is a
named list of six data frames (`status`, `metadata_status`, `frequency`,
`table_id`, `section`, and `surface_membership`), each with `facet`, `value`,
and `n` columns.

### IADB observations

With `format = "xml"`, `read_boe_series()` returns class `boe_iadb`, a list
with `metadata` and `observations`. Metadata has 16 columns:

```text
series_id, label, country, concatenated_label, frequency, frequency_code,
frequency_order, first_observation, last_observation, definition,
definition_url, category_name, category_value, category_label, category_order,
series_comment
```

Observations have 11 columns:

```text
series_id, date, value_raw, value, provisional_value_raw, provisional_value,
confidential, last_updated, last_revised, observation_comment, source_row
```

With `format = "csv"`, the result is a data frame with
`series_id`, `date`, `value_raw`, `value`, `suppressed`, and `source_row`.
Both formats carry `boe_provenance(x)`. XML is the canonical route when
metadata, footnotes, provisional values, or revision filtering matter.

### Bankstats, rates, and yields

`read_boe_bankstats_series(history = "full")` returns class
`boe_bankstats_series` with 31 columns, including the canonical observation
fields and exact source coordinates:

```text
series_id, period, date, date_precision, value, value_status, raw_value,
unit, seasonal_adjustment, release_date, source_table_id, source_member,
source_sheet, source_row, source_column, orientation, series_label,
series_frequency, series_country, concatenated_label, definition,
category_name, category_value, category_label, series_comment,
provisional_value_raw, provisional_value, confidential, last_updated,
last_revised, observation_comment
```

`history = "current_workbook"` returns the shorter rolling-window form (18
columns through `series_frequency`) when an exact workbook cell exists. A
time-across period keeps the official period label and an explicit period-start
date; the conversion is recorded in provenance.

`boe_bank_rate_history()` returns ten columns:
`period`, `date`, `date_precision`, `year`, `month`, `day`, `rate_raw`,
`rate`, `source_sheet`, and `source_row`. Month-only records keep `date = NA`.
`read_boe_yield_curve()` returns the long eight-column data frame
`date`, `maturity_years`, `rate_raw`, `rate`, `source_member`, `source_sheet`,
`source_row`, and `source_column`.

Successful network results carry a `boe_provenance` attribute containing the
source identity, canonical and final URLs, retrieval time, byte count and
SHA-256, validators when supplied, cache status, package version, and the
recorded transforms. Use `boe_provenance(x)` rather than relying on a URL alone.

## Common workflows

### IADB history and revisions

The following bounded live workflow is available for interactive use.
Documentation rendering uses the verified offline replay above so builds
remain deterministic.

```{r iadb-workflow, eval=FALSE}
deadline <- boe_deadline(45)

history <- read_boe_series(
  "IUDBEDR",
  from = "2024-01-01",
  to = "2024-01-31",
  format = "xml",
  deadline = deadline,
  max_bytes = 5 * 1024^2
)

history$metadata
history$observations
boe_provenance(history)

updates <- boe_series_updates(
  "IUMABEDR",
  from = "2025-01-01",
  to = "2025-12-31",
  updated_since = "latest",
  deadline = boe_deadline(45)
)
```

Use CSV when a downstream system requires a simple compatibility table. Use
XML when metadata, revision history, or footnotes are part of the analysis.

### Bankstats discovery and extraction

Use the offline catalogue to choose an identity, then choose the canonical
full-history route or the shorter rolling workbook route:

```{r bankstats-workflow, eval=FALSE}
asset <- boe_bankstats_assets(table_id = "A1.1.1", limit = 1)
bulk <- read_boe_bankstats(
  asset$url[[1]],
  member = "Latest Tables/TabA1.1.1.xls",
  deadline = boe_deadline(60)
)

full <- read_boe_bankstats_series(
  "LPMAVAB",
  table_id = "A1.1.1",
  history = "full",
  deadline = boe_deadline(60)
)

current_window <- read_boe_bankstats_series(
  "LPMAVAB",
  table_id = "A1.1.1",
  history = "current_workbook",
  deadline = boe_deadline(60)
)
```

Full history is backed by the canonical IADB bounds and can remain available
when a series is not chartable in the current workbook. The workbook route
requires an exact current cell and preserves its member, sheet, row, column,
and orientation.

### Bank Rate and yield curves

The registries are deterministic and can be inspected without a request. The
readers below use the official workbooks and ZIP files when called:

```{r rates-yields-workflow, eval=FALSE}
boe_rate_series()
bank_rate <- boe_bank_rate_history(deadline = boe_deadline(60))

yield_assets <- boe_yield_assets()
nominal <- read_boe_yield_curve(
  curve = "nominal",
  frequency = "monthly",
  scope = "archive",
  measure = "spot",
  deadline = boe_deadline(180)
)
```

Archive files may be revised upstream. The package records the selected asset,
curve, frequency, scope, measure, segment, member, sheet, and cell identity in
provenance; it does not turn an official daily series into a monthly average.

### Release registries and assets

`boe_release_registry()` is available offline. A release-asset read is only
valid after a verified `inst/extdata/release-assets.rds` snapshot has been
generated and committed; version 0.1.6 does not contain that file. Until that
is resolved, `boe_release_assets()` and
`read_boe_release_asset()` fail early with a typed `readboe_config` condition
rather than browsing an unpinned live page.

```{r releases-workflow, eval=FALSE}
boe_release_registry()

# After a verified release-assets snapshot is present:
assets <- boe_release_assets(
  family = "international_reserves",
  file_type = "xlsx"
)
raw <- read_boe_release_asset(assets$url[[1]], parse = "raw")
workbook <- read_boe_release_asset(assets$url[[1]], parse = "workbook")
```

Raw bytes are the fallback for heterogeneous official formats. Lossless
worksheet parsing is intentionally limited to XLS/XLSX.

## Network, deadlines, cache, and replay

Network readers use public Bank endpoints and require no credentials. They:

* use HTTPS and an allowlist of Bank of England hosts;
* apply a caller-owned absolute deadline across retries and parsing;
* enforce response, row, archive-member, workbook, cell, and output bounds;
* retry only transient failures with bounded attempts; and
* clean temporary files after parsing.

Success responses are cached under
`tools::R_user_dir("readboe", "cache")` by default. Cache entries are
hash-checked, TTL-bound, atomically written, pruned by entry count and total
bytes, and use only that managed location unless the caller explicitly
supplies another `cache_dir`. Set
`cache_only = TRUE` to replay an existing successful response without network
access; set `refresh = TRUE` to bypass a usable entry. `boe_cache_clear()`
removes only hash-named `readboe` entries in the directory supplied by the
caller.

For an application, pass one deadline through a workflow and retain the
provenance object with the result:

```r
deadline <- boe_deadline(60)
# result <- read_boe_series("IUDBEDR", deadline = deadline)
# replay <- read_boe_series("IUDBEDR", deadline = deadline, cache_only = TRUE)
# boe_provenance(replay)
```

## Scope and limitations

The bundled catalogue provides the audited identities linked from the
represented Bankstats page. At the snapshot date, 5,261 unique identities were
linked from the current Bankstats page, of which 5,252 passed the canonical
metadata and identity checks. Nine page links were excluded by the audit. Of
the 5,252 catalogue rows, 5,008 have an exact current-workbook occurrence and
244 are canonical-history-only; the latter remain valid for `history =
"full"`. The official current page exposes no historical bulk-ZIP archive, so
the workbook route is a rolling publication view.

Additional scope boundaries are:

* callers may request a known non-catalogued IADB identifier directly, while
  browse results remain scoped to the authenticated snapshot;
* dates are filtered inclusively, and month/quarter/year workbook labels retain
  explicit period starts and their official precision;
* official missing, suppressed, provisional, confidential, duplicate, and
  revision fields are retained rather than normalised away;
* aggregation, interpolation, gap filling, seasonal adjustment, and identity
  inference remain explicit downstream choices; and
* yield curves and downloaded release files remain subject to their source
  page's methodology, revisions, disclaimers, and reuse terms.

In version 0.1.6, the release-asset snapshot is missing, as described in
[Release registries and assets](#release-registries-and-assets). This is a
publication-readiness issue, not a reason to silently substitute a live,
unpinned page.

## Troubleshooting

Errors and warnings are typed so callers can make a deliberate retry, fallback,
or remediation decision. Inspect `class(condition)` and `conditionMessage(e)`.

| Condition | Typical cause | What to check |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `readboe_config` | Invalid argument, unsupported source combination, or missing release snapshot | Check argument choices, date order, `scope`/`frequency`, and required bundled files. |
| `readboe_bounds` | Response, row, cell, member, or output limit exceeded | Narrow the request or raise the relevant bound deliberately. |
| `readboe_identity_mismatch` | Requested ID/URL/member or authenticated snapshot does not match the declared identity | Rebuild from the exact catalogue/registry row; do not bypass the identity check. |
| `readboe_upstream_unavailable` | A page-listed identity has no exact current workbook cell | Use `history = "full"` or the canonical IADB reader. |
| `readboe_timeout` / `readboe_rate_limit` | Deadline expired or the upstream service asked the client to slow down | Retry later with a fresh deadline; use a cache-only replay when available. |
| `readboe_transport` | HTTPS, redirect, HTTP status, or connection failure | Check the official endpoint and network policy; credentials are not a fix. |
| `readboe_parse` / `readboe_schema_drift` | Malformed or changed upstream XML, CSV, ZIP, or workbook | Preserve the error and source identity for diagnosis; do not treat a partial parse as valid. |
| `readboe_cache_miss` / `readboe_cache_corruption` | No matching replay entry or a hash/identity check failed | Re-fetch when permitted, or clear only the affected managed cache entries. |

Bundled catalogue files under `inst/extdata/` are derived from Bank of England
Database/statistics pages. Reuse must follow the Bank's applicable legal terms
and any third-party terms. The Bank's legal notice identifies special handling
for selected exchange-rate series and for monetary-financial-institution data
relating to the Isle of Man, Guernsey, and Jersey. SONIA and SONIA Compounded
Index material requires the Bank-prescribed OGL v3.0 attribution and trademark
acknowledgement. Check
[`boe_rights()`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/man/boe_rights.Rd)
and the
[Bank of England Legal page](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/legal) before
redistributing source data. The package does not claim ownership of those
materials.

`readboe` is an independent client and is not endorsed by, affiliated with, or
sponsored by the Bank of England. Source links are provided for attribution
and verification. The package's primary author and maintainer is Chartwell Macro. For
reproducibility, cite the package version, the exact
series or asset identity, retrieval date, and `boe_provenance()` receipt. See
[`NEWS.md`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/NEWS.md) for changes
and
[`inst/CITATION`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/inst/CITATION),
or use GitHub's
[`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/CITATION.cff).

## Contributing and support

Email bug reports and reproducible upstream/schema observations to
[chartwellmacro@gmail.com](mailto:chartwellmacro@gmail.com). Include
the package version, R version/platform, exact function arguments, condition
class/message, source identity, and the provenance receipt where possible;
remove credentials and unrelated data before posting. Pull requests should
preserve raw-source fields, typed conditions, bounds, cache behaviour, and the
offline tests. Start with
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md),
[`NEWS.md`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/NEWS.md), the
[`docs/coverage-matrix.csv`](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe/blob/main/docs/coverage-matrix.csv),
and the repository's source before proposing a new surface or transformation.
